Tap repairs: symptoms and service choices

Tap drips after shut-off

A sealing component or another fitting fault may allow water through. A mixer leaking at its base is a different observation from a drip at the outlet. The fitting and parts need assessment before choosing repair or replacement.

Water lost through a persistent drip

A persistent drip wastes water, with the amount depending on its flow and duration. We do not estimate a saving from the sound alone; arrange assessment and compare the agreed repair or replacement option.

Installing a customer-supplied replacement mixer

Discuss the model and existing connection before purchase so the quote can identify installation, any additional parts and whether other access work is needed.

edits.after:
Water waste and customer-supplied mixers

A persistent drip wastes water; the amount depends on its flow and duration. A sealing component or another fitting fault may allow water through after shut-off, while water around a mixer base is a different observation. The fitting assessment described above establishes the affected component without estimating water savings from the sound alone.

For a customer-supplied replacement mixer, discuss the model before purchase. Its mounting and connection arrangement must suit the fixture. The quote separates installation, additional parts and any access work from the product itself, so a product-only price can be compared with the complete installation scope.

edits.before:
Water leak detection: symptoms and service choices

Hidden leaks and higher water bills

Water may escape where it is not readily visible, but a higher bill can also reflect changed use or other factors. Compare the timing and report meter observations; investigation is needed before attributing the bill to a concealed pipe leak.

Water-meter movement without expected use

Unexpected flow may indicate a leak or equipment still drawing water, including a running cistern. It does not by itself identify an underground leak. Follow Water Corporation guidance for meter concerns and arrange assessment of private plumbing where appropriate.

  • Water Corporation meter-leak guidance
edits.after:
Concealed leaks, water use and meter observations

A higher water bill may reflect a concealed leak, changed use or other factors. Compare the timing with visible moisture and available meter observations. Water-meter movement without expected use can also involve equipment still drawing water, such as a running cistern; it cannot locate an underground leak by itself.

Follow Water Corporation guidance for a concern at the meter or public supply. Investigation of private plumbing establishes the relevant source and repair scope. If the owner or managing agent needs findings, records or photographs from the visit, agree that requirement before booking.

  • Water Corporation meter-leak guidance
edits.reason: Merge educational topics into one substantive chapter
